messages:
Sara (CS): @Mike can you pick up Peridot Logistics' request? they want to onboard a custom NER that tags routing codes + addresses for shipment summaries. they mentioned PHI risk and want private deployment + HSM. pinging for scope/ETA.
Mike (SE): thx — any model details from them yet? size, framework, perf targets, qps? also do they need real-time (<=200ms) or async batching?
Sara (CS): customer replied in email: model is a fine-tuned T5-style 7B in PyTorch, trained on internal manifests (~12k labeled rows). target is ~50req/s peak, p95 latency <350ms acceptable, but they want prefix-caching and deterministic redaction for PII. they explicitly require KMS/HSM for keys and VPC/private control plane.
Eli (SRE): 7B with 50 qps on private infra -> rough estimate: 2x A100 equiv nodes with batching + compiled kernels; we should advise quantization to int8/4-bit to reduce mem. also need to confirm if they can tolerate sharded KV cache behavior (affects cold-start latency).
Mike (SE): sounds doable. questions for Peridot: 1) can they share sample eval set (2000 examples) with ground-truth tags? 2) are there legal constraints on retaining logs? 3) do they need on-prem package or VPC-private hosted?
Sara (CS): I'll ask. they said they prefer our Private VPC first, on-prem if regulatory review flags it. they can share a de-identified eval set but want us to run safety checks before we keep anything.
Jordan (Enablement): we should schedule a 1hr enablement call once infra decision made. suggest agenda: onboarding checklist, eval harness walkthrough, redaction > deterministic post-processing, rollback plan, renewal touchpoints. If takeover takes >8 weeks we flag renewal-risk for AE.
Mike (SE): for eval harness: we'll need labeled slices for PII classes (address, SSN, phone), and business-specific routing codes (approx 40 classes). ask them for an evaluation rubric: precision/recall per-class and a redaction false-negative threshold (ideally FN <0.2% for PII). also confirm acceptance criteria for model promotions.
Sara (CS): customer asked about automatic failover to a smaller open model to avoid downtime during bursts. can we support policy-based fallback (hosted/dedicated mix)?
Eli (SRE): yes — we can route by policy. fallback to a distil 1-2B model is possible but must be in the same contract env (private/dedicated). caveat: output shape mismatch for some tags — need a normalization layer. we'll add a transform hook.
Mike (SE): I'll draft a recommended config for them. quick sketch:
```
model: peridot-ner-7b
deployment:
  mode: private-vpc
  nodes: 2
  quantization: int8
  caching: prefix_kv
security:
  kms: customer-hsm
  audit_logs_retention: 90d
routing:
  fallback: peridot-ner-distil-1b
  policy: latency<=400ms, cost_threshold
``` 
Mike (SE): also propose a staged rollout: canary with 5% traffic for 48h + quality eval on their gold set, then 25% / 72h, then full. add automatic rollback on quality regression >2% absolute F1 drop on critical PII classes.
Sara (CS): Customer asked about cost guidance. Jordan / finance pls advise on order-of-magnitude monthly reserved cost vs pay-as-you-go. they want a committed plan if rolling to Dedicated later.
Jordan (Enablement): I'll coordinate with finance but give them a ballpark: Private VPC 7B w/ reserved nodes ~ $$$/mo (ballpark) vs hosted burst cheaper but less compliant. I'll confirm exact figures. also will prep an enablement invite for next week — proposing Tue 10am PT.
onboard-bot: checklist created -> /runbooks/onboarding/peridot-1969999999, assigned to Sara (CS), Mike (SE), Eli (SRE)
Sara (CS): next actions for us:
- Mike: draft deployment + eval config and acceptance criteria (by EOD Fri)
- Eli: capacity sketch + fallback normalization plan (by Mon)
- Jordan: schedule enablement + cost estimate (by Mon)
I'll ask Peridot for eval files and data retention constraints. tagging @AE to keep renewal awareness.
Mike (SE): will do. small note: ask if they require deterministic redaction (exact token masking) vs probabilistic tagging — affects design.
Sara (CS): noted. I'll clarify. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
